title: Google Cloud Platform
description: Production Google Cloud reference covering organizations, folders, projects, IAM, service accounts, networking, compute, Kubernetes, serverless, storage, databases, messaging, observability, security, reliability, cost, infrastructure as code, and incident readiness.

subtopics.title: Organizations, Folders & Projects
subtopics.description: Resources belong to projects, projects can be grouped under folders, and organization policies inherit down the hierarchy. Projects provide billing, quota, API, IAM, and lifecycle boundaries.

diagram.content:
flowchart TD
  Org["Organization"] --> Security["Security folder"]
  Org --> Prod["Production folder"]
  Org --> NonProd["Non-production folder"]
  Prod --> P1["Project: checkout-prod"]
  NonProd --> P2["Project: checkout-dev"]

callouts.title: Use Projects as Deliberate Boundaries
callouts.text: Separate environments, teams, data sensitivity, blast radius, billing, and lifecycle where appropriate. Avoid one giant project or uncontrolled project sprawl.

subtopics.title: IAM, Service Accounts & Federation
subtopics.description: Grant roles to principals at the narrowest useful resource scope. Prefer workload and workforce federation or attached service identities over exported service-account keys.

callouts.title: Service Account Is Both Identity and Resource
callouts.text: Control who may impersonate, attach, or create keys for it, not only which permissions the account itself has.

subtopics.title: Organization Policy, Secret Manager & Cloud KMS
subtopics.description: Use organization constraints for guardrails, Secret Manager for versioned application secrets, and Cloud KMS for managed encryption keys and envelope-encryption workflows.

codeBlocks.code:
gcloud projects get-iam-policy <project-id>
gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=app-config
gcloud kms keys list --location=global --keyring=platform

callouts.title: Encryption Does Not Replace Authorization
callouts.text: Key and secret access are high-value permissions. Separate administrators, rotate versions, log access, protect deletion, and test recovery without exposing plaintext.

subtopics.title: VPC, Subnets, Routes, Firewall & Private Access
subtopics.description: Google Cloud VPC networks are global while subnets are regional. Routes choose paths; hierarchical and VPC firewall policies filter traffic; private access patterns control service reachability and egress.

codeBlocks.code:
Internet → global/regional load balancer → managed instance group or serverless NEG
Private workloads → Cloud NAT for controlled egress
Private Google API access → Private Google Access / PSC where applicable
Hybrid → Cloud VPN or Interconnect + Cloud Router/BGP

callouts.title: Firewall Rules Do Not Prove Application Reachability
callouts.text: Also verify routes, tags/service accounts, load-balancer health, DNS, NAT, organization policy, application bind address, and return path.

subtopics.title: Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud Run & Functions
subtopics.description: Choose by control needs, workload shape, portability, scaling latency, request/event semantics, accelerator needs, and platform operating cost.

rows: Workloads plus chosen cluster mode responsibilities

callouts.title: Serverless Still Has Limits
callouts.text: Design for concurrency, cold starts, request duration, CPU/memory, connection pools, filesystem ephemerality, retries, and scale-up pressure on downstream systems.

subtopics.title: Load Balancing, Cloud DNS & Cloud CDN
subtopics.description: Select global or regional load balancing from protocol, backend, locality, sovereignty, failover, and source-IP needs. Treat DNS TTL and CDN cache policy as deployment contracts.

codeBlocks.code:
Client → Cloud DNS → external Application Load Balancer
                    → Cloud Armor policy
                    → Cloud CDN cache
                    → regional backends with health checks

callouts.title: Health Checks Need a Stable Contract
callouts.text: Keep them fast and independent from nonessential dependencies. Test draining, unhealthy backend removal, failover, cache behavior, and certificate renewal.

subtopics.title: Cloud Storage, Persistent Disk & Filestore
subtopics.description: Cloud Storage is object storage, Persistent Disk/Hyperdisk provide VM block storage, and Filestore provides managed shared NFS. Pick location, durability, access, lifecycle, and consistency semantics deliberately.

codeBlocks.code:
gcloud storage cp artifact.tar.gz gs://example-artifacts/releases/
gcloud storage objects describe gs://example-artifacts/releases/artifact.tar.gz

callouts.title: Object Storage Is Not POSIX Storage
callouts.text: Use immutable objects, generations/preconditions, checksums, resumable upload, lifecycle rules, and explicit cache metadata instead of filesystem assumptions.

subtopics.title: Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Spanner, Firestore, Bigtable & BigQuery
subtopics.description: Choose data services from transactions, relational constraints, access keys, horizontal scale, analytics, latency, consistency, and operational requirements.

callouts.title: Managed Does Not Mean Maintenance-Free
callouts.text: Plan schema migrations, capacity, quotas, backup/restore, failover, client retries, connection management, upgrades, and data residency.

subtopics.title: Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks, Eventarc & Workflows
subtopics.description: Pub/Sub provides asynchronous fan-out, Cloud Tasks schedules controlled HTTP delivery, Eventarc routes events, and Workflows orchestrates explicit multi-step service calls.

codeBlocks.code:
Pub/Sub: durable asynchronous event distribution and subscriptions
Cloud Tasks: per-target delivery rate, schedule, retry and task identity
Eventarc: event routing from supported sources to destinations
Workflows: stateful orchestration, retries, branching and compensation

callouts.title: Assume Duplicate Delivery
callouts.text: Make handlers idempotent, ack only after committed effects, bound retries, classify poison events, retain correlation IDs, and operate dead-letter recovery.

subtopics.title: Cloud Monitoring, Logging, Trace & Audit Logs
subtopics.description: Define service-level indicators and alerts, centralize logs, correlate traces, retain administrative/data-access audit evidence according to risk, and route security findings to owners.

codeBlocks.code:
User SLI/SLO → burn-rate alerts → runbook and owner
Metrics + logs + traces + deploy markers → incident correlation
Cloud Audit Logs + asset/config findings → protected central project
Security Command Center findings → triage and response workflow

callouts.title: Control Log Volume and Sensitive Data
callouts.text: Logging exclusions reduce cost but can remove evidence. Define mandatory security/operations data and prevent credentials or personal payloads from entering telemetry.

subtopics.title: Availability, Backup & Disaster Recovery
subtopics.description: Design zonal and regional failure behavior from explicit RPO/RTO. Use multi-zone first, add multi-region only when requirements justify data, routing, consistency, and operational complexity.

codeBlocks.code:
Failure modes: instance, zone, region, identity, quota, dependency, bad deploy
RPO → replication + backup/PITR frequency
RTO → detection + failover + restore + validation time
Drill → isolate, restore, switch traffic, verify data, communicate, fail back

callouts.title: Replication Is Not Backup
callouts.text: Deletes, corruption, and compromised credentials can replicate. Maintain protected independent backups and prove restoration into an isolated environment.

subtopics.title: IaC, Quotas, Cost & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Manage resources through reviewed infrastructure as code, budgets, labels, policy checks, quota planning, progressive delivery, and ownership metadata.

codeBlocks.code:
gcloud config configurations list
gcloud projects describe <project-id>
gcloud services list --enabled --project <project-id>
gcloud billing budgets list --billing-account <billing-account-id>

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Structure projects/folders, federate identity, avoid service-account keys, enforce guardrails, use private networking, design multi-zone, encrypt and back up, centralize audit/telemetry, plan quotas, tag ownership, scan IaC, set budgets, and rehearse incidents.
